key_concepts: A transverse wave has oscillations perpendicular to the direction of wave motion.
Crest is the highest point and trough is the lowest point of a wave.
Amplitude is the height of a wave.
Wavelength is the distance from crest to crest or trough to trough.
Period is the time to complete one wave cycle; frequency is the number of cycles per unit
Water surface waves are predominantly transverse but also have a longitudinal component.
Rope waves show rhythmic up-and-down motion and a sinusoidal shape.

Increasing the speed of up-and-down rope motion increases wave frequency.
Regular ocean waves get energy from wind, while tsunamis get energy from underwater earthq
Electromagnetic waves are transverse and can travel without a medium, unlike water waves.
Electromagnetic waves are used in telecommunications, cooking, and medical sciences.
